title: Pruning preserves outputs outside a subprotocol
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, and let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$. Suppose $s$ is a subprotocol of $p$ and has strictly fewer leaves than $p$. For any $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$ such that the pair $(x,y)$ does not reach $s$ (that is, $x$ or $y$ fails one of the corresponding branching conditions along the path to $s$), deleting the branch leading to $s$ from $p$ leaves its output on $(x,y)$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ and $p$ are protocols over these input and output types
$(x,y)$ does not reach $s$ under the chosen path
replaced:
Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over Alice's inputs
$X$, Bob's inputs $Y$, and output type $\alpha$, and suppose $s$ is a subprotocol of $p$
(a rooted subtree) whose leaf count is strictly smaller than that of $p$. Form the
pruned protocol obtained by deleting the subtree $s$ from $p$. Then for every pair of
inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$ that does not reach $s$ — that is, $(x,y)$ fails to be
consistent with all of the branching choices along the path from the root of $p$ down to
$s$ — the pruned protocol and $p$ produce the same output on $(x,y)$: running the pruned
protocol on $x$ and $y$ yields exactly $p$'s output on $x$ and $y$.
